hardware: 8 GPU per node, NVLink in-node, 400 Gb/s IB per-GPU rail cross-node
calibration_domain: calibrated on a production multimodal transformer whose shape is withheld; the shipped profile module (usp_calib_v1.py) pairs this table with a synthetic example shape, so absolute example outputs illustrate the pipeline rather than reproduce the production system

methodology.E2: offline a2a collective microbenchmark sweep + full-grid collective-only attribution rerun
methodology.E3: offline ring per-hop benchmark (R=2 and R=4 lanes)
methodology.E4: offline compute kernel sweeps (FA / GEMM / MoE rate curves)
methodology.E6: ring overlap precheck (backward chunk counts K in {1, 2, 4})
methodology.E7: global residual calibration (profilers-off segment vs rank-max busy reconciliation)
methodology.E9: static tier sweeps on heterogeneous data (fwd KV exposure vs rho LUT, sp32 closure fix)
methodology.E10: in-train a2a inflation reconciliation (per-tier measured/curve fits)
methodology.E11: kernel-level attribution (FA long-seg flatness, MoE rate re-anchor, gamma decomposition)

a2a.law: t_ms = max(floor, t0 + bytes/BW); one call per direction (pre=QKV, post=O) per attention per microbatch
a2a.scope_note: curve includes tensor_split/contiguous/cat host copies (full all_to_all_tensor); in-train collective-only is faster (~700 GB/s implied), so this curve is a safe, slightly conservative upper bound. No in-train degradation (NVLink unaffected by FSDP/NIC traffic).
a2a.exposure: fully exposed on critical path (no overlap); in-train totals 2.37s (sp16) / 2.97s (sp8) per rank-step in the anchor runs
a2a.held_out_err_attribution: worst 8.2% is model-form error at the floor->linear knee (0.5-4x knee bytes: |err| p50 2.4% max 8.2%); floor region p50 0.4%, linear region p50 0.2%. Not noise, not copies. Full-grid collective-only rerun: host copies = ~55-58% of floor and 32-69% of slope (pre worse than post); pure-collective NVLink BW 888-1570 GB/s. Per-point jitter (p90-p10)/p50: a2a ~0.18-0.27 vs ring P2P 0.011, so the a2a fit floor is percent-level by nature. Curve unchanged: production U8 large messages sit in the linear region; the knee region corresponds to high-sp small buckets, already flagged conservative.
a2a.in_train_inflation_note: T_a2a(in-train) = curve(bytes) x factor(tier). up_a2a completion includes waiting for U-group peers. Skew source: per-rank SPEED differences (in-group machine downclocking, confirmed via per-rank rate telemetry; measured ~6% systematic FA-rate spread, slow ranks stable across steps) -- NOT load imbalance (packing splits each sample evenly across sp ranks; in-group FA flops measured exactly equal). Monotone in R: absolute skew grows with compute between syncs while per-call bytes/baseline shrink. Fit: measured/curve on full per-step up_a2a totals -- sp8 1.467/1.415 (two independent runs), sp16 1.908 (homogeneous)/1.931 (heterogeneous), sp32 3.034 (homogeneous)/2.978 (heterogeneous); cross-dataset stable within 2%. Supersedes the older per-call-p50 'in-train is faster' reconciliation (E10); the skew mechanism was corrected after the initial fit.

ring.law: per-hop completion t_ms = t0 + bytes/BW; bytes = tuple bytes (KV: K+V+cu_seqlens; dKV: dK+dV, pre-chunked /K)
ring.validity: R=2 and R=4 both measured offline (67MB-1.21GB per hop, linear regime); R=4 curve identical to R=2 within noise (kv t0 0.231/48.7, dkv t0 0.17-0.18/48.7-48.8) -> per-hop completion cost is ring-size independent, reuse the R=2 fits for any R
ring.exposure_rule: R=2: only bwd dKV tail exposed: T_ring_exposed ~= N_layer x beta(chunk_bytes) x (t0_dkv + tuple_bytes/(K x BW_dkv)); fwd KV / bwd KV / dKV middle fully hidden (<0.2% step); exposed fraction of tail chunks = 1/K exactly. R=4 adds a fwd KV term, see sp32_R4.
ring.hidden_terms_validity: bwd KV / dKV middle = 0 only inside the validity domain: bwd KV hiding budget is 2.5x flops at equal bytes -> its own threshold ~0.4x of the fwd one (s_bar >= ~0.4 x R x 41.7K); dKV middle threshold is another ~K lower. Production s_bar gives 4-10x margin; if solver buckets push s_bar below ~0.4x threshold these terms start exposing and the model is out of domain.

beta_by_chunk_bytes.note: amplification of exposed wait vs offline completion; grows as chunks shrink (t0-type overhead + peer launch delay dominate); keys were K={1,2,4}@sp16 and K=4@sp32. Composition sensitivity (E9): on the heterogeneous dataset beta runs ~25% higher at comparable chunk bytes (266MB: 2.63, 132MB: 2.59) -- more intra-bucket length variance widens per-hop jitter; treat values as p50 with +25% band on heterogeneous data

fwdkv_exposure_frac_by_rho.note: E9: fraction of fwd KV hop waits exposed (>1ms) vs rho = s_bar/threshold, from STATIC sp16/sp32 sweeps on the heterogeneous dataset. Exposure decays smoothly with rho (ramp, not cliff): R=2 reaches ~0 only at rho>=3.5; R=4 unmeasured beyond 1.52 (extrapolate with R2 decay shape, low confidence). Below first knot: clamp (unmeasured, low confidence). Exposed wait ~= 0.85 x offline completion (both tiers). Per layer: frac x (R-1) x 0.85 x completion. impl: USPCalibV1Profile._ring_fwdkv_exposed_ms(hop_bytes, R, rho). A lower-variance static dataset sat 6-12% lower at equal rho -- heterogeneous intra-bucket variance adds exposure; this LUT is the conservative (heterogeneous) calibration.

overlap_min_seg_tokens.rule: fwd KV hop fully hidden iff FLOPs-weighted mean segment length s_bar = sum(s_i^2)/S_bucket >= R x (c_kv/(4 Hq d)) x P_fa_eff/BW_eff; the prefactor c_kv/(4 Hq d) equals 1.0 at the production shape (validated on sp16/sp32 in-train hop bytes) and also at the shipped synthetic shape. Threshold depends ONLY on per-segment length, not bucket total.
overlap_min_seg_tokens.cross_check: production natural s_bar 140-168K: sp16 1.7x above threshold -> fwd KV 93% hidden; sp32 right at threshold -> 1/3 hops exposed (E6). Solver: use as bucketing constraint with ~30% headroom; bwd threshold ~0.4x of fwd (not binding); dKV tail exposure is length-independent (mitigate via K only).

sp32_R4.basis: static sp32 30-step run (U8 x R4, K=4); supersedes the short-sample hot-switch preview
sp32_R4.dkv_tail: rule transfers: exposed frac 30.8% (~1/K), beta 2.5 @149MB chunks, contributes 1.93s/rank-step
sp32_R4.fwd_kv: first-class exposed term at R>=4: exposed frac 32.6% (~1/(R-1) hops), exposed wait ~0.87x completion, contributes 2.03s/rank-step; model as T_fwdkv_exposed ~= N_layer x (t0_kv + bytes_hop/BW_kv) per microbatch
sp32_R4.total: ring exposure p50 4.25s/rank-step = ~4.5% of the 94.6s step (sp16 K=4: 1.4%)

ring.fa_cache_note: fa-cache IS wired and active on the ring path (the ring attention varlen cache accessor): AC replay skips fwd ring loop + FA. bwd KV rotations seen in backward are the backward pass's own ring loop (dq/dkv needs KV), not a recompute.

compute.law: T = FLOPs / (P_plateau x eta_P(x)) with eta LUT (log-interp) from the offline compute sweep; or FA additive law below

fa_additive_law.form: T_ms = FLOPs / P + c_seg x n_seg; FLOPs_fwd = 4 x Hq x d x sum(qi x ki), FLOPs_bwd = 2.5 x FLOPs_fwd
fa_additive_law.validity: n_seg <= ~1000; production n_seg ~9-10; fitted at the production attention shape; per-segment coverage 128-196K tokens (plateau holds to 196K)
fa_additive_law.long_seg_note: E11 D-series: fixed-total varlen sweep, per-seg 8K-512K x nseg 1-64 -> fwd 1475-1505 / bwd 1186-1285 TF/s, completely flat. No efficiency decay past 8K per segment; the apparent sag past 8K in an earlier series is a shrinking-total (underfeeding) confound of that series' fixed-ssq design.

compute.moe_intrain_rule: T_moe_fwd = flops_est / moe_intrain_rate_tflops (847 TF/s, in-train anchor); flops_est = the model's per-token MoE forward FLOPs (the production value is withheld; the shipped profile module uses a synthetic example constant); rate flat vs tokens (chunk-capped) ONLY for per-rank routed tokens >= 16384; below the chunk size use moe_rate_lut (log-interp) instead of the flat rate
compute.moe_rate_note: in-train anchor: p50 of ~1.3M in-train MoE forward kernel events across nodes, +-4% node-uniform (E11). The ONLY trustworthy absolute MoE rate: offline plateaus are kernel-autotune-state dependent (an earlier offline baseline was an unreproducible outlier; a same-host re-run came out 23% lower; the knee SHAPE is still usable). The legacy OF_moe=1.25 factor (= 1059 outlier baseline / 847) was REMOVED from this table as misleading -- neither 1059 nor 1.25 has standalone meaning.

moe_rate_lut.comment: below-knee fallback, re-anchored per E11: values = the earlier offline sweep's relative shape x 847 TF/s in-train anchor (spliced continuously at 16384). Rationale: absolute offline rates are autotune-state dependent (two full sweeps disagree BOTH in level and shape, crossing at ~4K: the later sweep measured 293/459/604/691/750 -- faster at low tokens, lower plateau, earlier knee ~8-10K). The steeper earlier shape is kept as the CONSERVATIVE choice for solver penalties; the later shape serves as an upper-bound reference. In-train anchors only cover >=16.4K tokens, so the sub-16K region remains offline-only confidence.

in_train_overhead_factors.moe: REMOVED: the legacy OF_moe=1.25 lived here; MoE now uses compute.moe_intrain_rate_tflops (847) directly, see moe_rate_note
in_train_overhead_factors.note: OF x law prediction = in-train time; FA measured on sp16 ring chunks (166k/664k events) and sp8 fa-cache packed (83k events), p10-p90 within +-7%

global.C_global_note: E7 segment B (profilers off, 100 steps): step p50 83.2s vs segment A rank-max busy p50 82.1s -> clean C_global ~1.1-2.4s, v1 uses 2.0s (~2.5% of step). Earlier static 5.5s residual included ~3s profiler/recorder overhead. Instrumentation perturbation ~1.1s (1.3%, within data noise).
global.periodic_spikes: RESOLVED: with profilers off no periodic structure remains; remaining +-15% step scatter is natural batch composition variance (not a cost model term)

gamma_comp.definition: gamma = measured block busy / modeled compute; model_fwd = FA_law_fwd + MoE_rule; model_bwd = 2.5x FA_law_bwd + 3x MoE_rule for ALL tiers -- fa-cache is active on the ring path too (AC replay restores cached out/lse, skips fwd ring loop + FA kernels; verified by event counts), so there is NO FA fwd-recompute term. MoE flops convention: the in-train MoE forward counter fires on chunked fwd AND AC replay, so single-forward = recorded/2.

pure_compute.usage: USE THIS with explicit T_a2a + T_ring_exposed terms (comm exposure subtracted from busy before fitting: all up_a2a wait + ring wait > 1ms)

comm_inclusive.usage: block-level shortcut: gamma x (FA+MoE) already contains intra-block a2a/ring exposure; do NOT add explicit comm terms on top

gamma_comp.recommended: pure_compute per-mode + explicit comm terms (matches the documented time model); single-number fallback 0.87 (pure) / 0.90 (inclusive)
gamma_comp.basis: fit with the comm-subtracted convention (MoE/2, no fa-recompute); each tier fit on one homogeneous run and cross-checked on one heterogeneous run
gamma_comp.note: gamma > 1: unmodeled ops (projections/norms/glue) put measured busy above the FA+MoE-only model; stable across datasets (hetero crosschecks within ~4%). v1.1 recalibration: previous v1 gammas (<1) were fit with two convention errors that partially cancelled (MoE replay flops double-counted; phantom FA fwd-recompute term on ring tiers). Closure replay revalidated after the fix.
gamma_comp.kernel_attribution: E11 (profiler-trace attribution on three ranks, mutually consistent): unmodeled kernels = 20-25% of modeled (FA+MoE) time, same order as gamma-1 (side-stream copies explain the gap). Breakdown of unmodeled: projection GEMMs (bf16) ~31%, copies/concat incl. FSDP staging ~20%, fp32 SIMT GEMMs ~18% (per-block conditioning/modulation on a non-tensor-core f32 path, 1.6-2s/rank-step -- optimization candidate), elementwise glue ~12%, router topk ~8%, fused attn-res + norm/rope ~12%.

global.C_switch_note: measured on the heterogeneous mixed-tier dataset (E8, 47 steps, ~half of them switch steps across sp8/16/32 mixes): switch vs non-switch wall p50 within +0.3/-1.5s of each other, buried in +-10s batch variance -> C_switch ~ 0, conservative upper bound 1.5s (<3% step). Model as 0; keep 1.5s inside the C_global uncertainty band if headroom needed.

gamma_hetero_crosscheck.note: E8 mixed-tier pure_compute fit; same family as sp8 (0.855/0.879) -> kernel calibration is dataset-independent

global.closure_all_datasets: step-level closure p50 across the seven calibration/validation runs: -1.0%, -2.8%, -3.3%, -0.3% (heterogeneous mixed), +0.3%, +4.0%, +4.6%. All within +-5%; sp32 slightly conservative (overpredicts).
global.pending: larger-scale C_global recheck (the anchor-scale window cannot reach the production per-GPU batch: the gradient-accumulation path crashes, and the single-microbatch setting exhausts fa-cache pinned host memory -> NCCL watchdog timeout); R=2 fwdkv exposure below rho 1.5 and R=4 above rho 1.52 (needs controlled replay); MoE cross-node rate spread mechanism unpinned (E11: -26..-34% on one node with FA unchanged; remeasure the in-train MoE rate per node window)

validity_domain.topology: measured on a multi-node anchor window; a2a in-node U<=8; ring cross-node R in {2, 4} (offline curves identical; in-train exposure structure measured for both)
validity_domain.data: natural production batches + a heterogeneous mixed-tier dataset (E8: closure and gamma transfer without refit); controlled length-bucket replay not yet done
